Costco has charged $1.50 for a hot dog and soda since the 1980s 🌭

The deal loses money on paper, and the co-founder reportedly warned: "If you raise the effing hot dog, I will kill you. Figure it out."
Why hold the price? Because the real profit is the membership card: $5.3 billion in fees in fiscal 2025, about half of Costco's operating income.
Costco even built its own hot dog to protect the price: Kirkland Signature franks since 2009, and cost cuts on the drinks too.
One cheap product can sell the whole store.

Ryanair's average fare is about €46. Its extras bring in almost 3x its profit ✈️

In the year to March 2025, Ryanair earned €4.7 billion from extras like bags, seats and priority boarding.
That's about a third of its €13.95 billion revenue, against a profit after tax of €1.61 billion.
Gate staff have reportedly been offered bonuses for spotting oversized bags.
The ticket gets you in. The choices pay the bills.
